simple.meaning: צְלָא (tsᵉlâʼ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “pray.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Ezra, Daniel, beginning at Ezra 6:10. The surrounding contexts include family line, sacrifice, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to צְלָא (H6739) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: צְלָא (tsᵉlâʼ) / H6739 is traced through Ezra 6:10, Daniel 6:11 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H6739. tsela [ צְלָא ] verb Pa`el pray (originally bow in prayer) ( ᵑ7 id., bow , Pa`el pray , so Syriac and Pa.; Assyrian ƒullû , entreat (apparently not of prayer to gods Zim KAT 3. 610 f. ); Arabic middle of the back , II. pray , Ethiopic bow , pray ; Sabean צלות shrine Hom Chr 125; AA 185 ); — Participle מְצַלֵּא Dan 6:11 (absolute); plural מְצַלַּ֫יִן (K § 47a )) Ezra 6:10 (with ל in behalf of ).
definitions.rootNote: (Aramaic) probably corresponding to 6760 in the sense of bowing;

occurrences.englishText: that they may offer sacrifices of pleasant aroma to the God of heaven, and pray for the life of the king, and of his sons.
Then these men assembled together, and found Daniel making petition and supplication before his God.
